_meta.description: Independent literature ranges that model OUTPUTS are checked against. These are deliberately NOT model inputs - they are the acceptance criteria.
_meta.usage: src/validation/literature_check.py compares each model output against min/max and reports PASS / WARN / FAIL.

targets.label: Iron ore consumption
targets.source: CEEW (Nitturu et al. 2024): pellets 1.4-1.5, peaking at 1.6 t-ore/t-DRI. Dey et al. (2015) measured 1.587.
targets.note: Lump-ore operation is 1.8-2.0 t-ore/t-DRI and will correctly fail this pellet-based band.

targets.label: Coal consumption
targets.source: CEEW (Nitturu et al. 2024): imported coal 0.9-1.1, domestic coal 1.4-1.6 t-coal/t-DRI.

targets.label: Specific energy consumption
targets.source: Lower bound from TERI: 5.54 Gcal/t-iron at 89% Fe = 4.93 Gcal/t-DRI, assuming imported coal at 0.95 t/t and 5,200 kcal/kg. Upper bound from BEE: 0.64-0.82 toe/t = 6.4-8.2 Gcal/t for the MSME sector. Dey et al. (2015) measured 6.26 Gcal/t-DRI (118.4 Gcal/h coal NHV at 18.9 t/h).
targets.note: The band is deliberately wide because the literature spans imported coal (~0.95 t/t, low SEC) and high-ash domestic coal (1.4-1.6 t/t, high SEC). Narrow it once the coal grade for the case study is fixed.

targets.label: DRI total iron
targets.source: Dey et al. (2015) Table 7: Fe (total) 92.5%. TERI assumes 89% iron content in sponge iron.

targets.label: Degree of metallisation
targets.source: Bhardwaj et al.: 'metallization of higher than 88%'; 'metallization rate of 89-90%'; 'metallization of 91'. Dey et al. Table 7 implies 83.5/92.5 = 90.3%.

targets.label: Direct (stack) CO2 intensity
targets.source: Lower bound from Nduagu et al.: rotary kiln DRI life-cycle 1391-1880 kgCO2e/t-DRI (1880 base case without export credit, 1590 net of 351 kWh/t-DRI WHR export), which corresponds to an imported-coal rate near 0.95 t/t. Upper bound scales that carbon balance to CEEW's surveyed domestic-coal rate of 1.4-1.6 t-coal/t-DRI.
targets.note: CO2 intensity is close to linear in the coal rate, so this band is wide by construction. Judge a run against the part of the band matching its coal grade, not against the midpoint.

targets.label: Auxiliary power
targets.source: CEEW (Nitturu et al. 2024): 55-65 kWh/t-DRI typical, 80-100 kWh/t-DRI for some plants.

targets.label: WHR gross generation
targets.source: Nduagu et al.: 450-451 kWh/t-DRI generated; 351 kWh/t-DRI exported after in-plant use.
targets.note: Boiler efficiency 60% and stack 150 C are BEE 2019; cycle efficiency 0.2265 is derived from the BEE 2011 DPR heat balance (Annexure 2). Model 0.3.0 used an unsourced 0.25 and sat just above this band. None of these is a measured boiler test.

targets.label: WHR surplus export
targets.source: Nduagu et al.: 'the exported power of 351 kWh/t-DRI'.
targets.note: Export is what remains after the kiln's own power demand and the BEE 2011 auxiliary fraction of 10%. It falls inside this band with the BEE 2019 heat-exchanger efficiency and the cycle efficiency derived from the BEE 2011 DPR.

targets.label: Waste-gas sensible heat share
targets.source: Dey et al. (2015) Table 11 item [13e]: waste-gas sensible heat 28.3 Gcal/h against coal NHV input of 118.4 Gcal/h = 23.9%.
targets.note: Expressed against coal NHV. Against Dey's 'reaction heat' figure of 64.98 Gcal/h the same term is 43.6%, which is the number usually quoted.

targets.label: H2 for complete DR (reference only)
targets.source: Kamal et al.: validated against 53.5-59.6 kg/t DRI, model yields 55.7, design value 59.6 kg H2/t DRI.
targets.note: INFORMATIONAL, not an acceptance criterion. The model reports the STOICHIOMETRIC hydrogen for the oxygen actually removed at 90.2% metallisation, which is ~47 kg/t. Kamal et al.'s 53.5-59.6 kg/t is for complete reduction and their 59.6 is explicitly 'a more conservative design value ... to account for operational inefficiencies, performance degradation and uncertainties'. A model value 10-20% below the band is therefore the expected result, and confirms the stoichiometry rather than contradicting it.
